numerical_failure.observed_behavior: The cache hash in _get_components_and_classes includes the raw self.wcs.equinox value. When equinox is NaN, the NaN != NaN comparison defeats the cache, so the cache check does not match as intended and wcs.world_axis_object_components is not reused.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Caching of wcs.world_axis_object_components and world_axis_object_classes should work when equinox is NaN; the NaN is normalized (replaced by None in the hash via None if np.isnan(equinox) else equinox) so the cache comparison succeeds and repeated accesses return the same cached object.

category_specific_evidence: The regression test test_components_and_classes_cache asserts that wcs.world_axis_object_components is wcs.world_axis_object_components when equinox is undefined (NaN), checking cache hit identity.
The cache key included self.wcs.equinox directly; NaN compares unequal to itself (NaN != NaN), so the cache comparison never hit when equinox was NaN.
The fix normalizes equinox to None when np.isnan(equinox), so the wcs_hash tuple compares equal across calls.

The bug is a caching/identity defect caused by NaN self-inequality rather than a formula or numerical-value error; no mathematical formula or concrete numeric expected/actual values are given in the passages.
reproduction_risks: Passages do not state a dtype, precision, magnitude regime, or tolerance; the reproduction relies on equinox being NaN (undefined) in WCS(naxis=2) with ctype RA---TAN and DEC--TAN.
The check is object identity of cached results rather than a numerical comparison, so numerical tolerance does not apply.
